lesson_title: Mapwork Paper Practice Run: The Real November 2018 Questions, Marked Like the Memo
hook_text: This exact gradient question appeared on a real matric paper — and the memo paid five marks for five lines. Watch them land.
clip_script: A real national exam question: calculate the average gradient between contour line O, height eight hundred and twenty metres, and the trigonometrical station at P on World's View. Step one, vertical interval: one thousand and fifty-seven comma nine minus eight hundred and twenty — two hundred and thirty-seven comma nine metres. Step two, horizontal equivalent: three comma nine centimetres on the map, at one to fifty thousand that is one thousand nine hundred and fifty metres. Step three, substitute and divide: one in eight comma two. The memo paid a mark for each step — the interval, the measurement, the equivalent, the substitution, the ratio — and even accepted a millimetre of ruler difference. Working shown, five out of five.
visual_style: Exam answer sheet filling line by line over a sketched contour slope up to a trig beacon: each written step stamps +1 as it lands, ending on 5/5 with the memo's accepted range 1:7,9 to 1:8,4 shown as a green band.
pacing: Methodical beats, one per calculation step, with a quick payoff montage of the five marks landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full practice run and answer the rest of the real 2018 mapwork paper.
